blocks.section: Risk of fire and/or smoke
blocks.content: Flames and/or smoke may come out of the oven when switching it on after service/repair. This can be caused by a defective electrical component or electrical connections (wiring) that have been refitted incorrectly.

blocks.section: Risk of fire and/or smoke
blocks.content:  Switch off the oven.

blocks.section: Risk of fire and/or smoke
blocks.content:  Disconnect/isolate the oven from the electrical supply.

blocks.section: Risk of fire and/or smoke
blocks.content:  Keep the oven door closed to stifle any flames.

Process for carrying out modification / change:
blocks.content: Cool down the oven then isolate from the mains supply by disconnecting the plug and fitting a suitable 'locking off' device or  locking in the off position the isolation switch if the oven is hard wired. Ensure your proprietary voltage tester is working correctly  and prove the mains supply is dead

blocks.section: Process for carrying out modification / change:
blocks.content: Wait 5 Minutes to allow the capacitor to  naturally discharge its energy.

blocks.section: Process for carrying out modification / change:
blocks.content: It is recommended that you stand on electrically safe matting where possible.

blocks.section: Process for carrying out modification / change:
blocks.content:  Remove the lid and side panels to access the oven components

blocks.section: Process for carrying out modification / change:
blocks.content:  Connect the capacitor discharge probe's earth clip to the equipotential   bonding point / casing at the rear of the oven

blocks.section: Process for carrying out modification / change:
blocks.content: Hold the probe against the HV capacitor terminal for 5 seconds, removing any covers to do so. Repeat on the other set of terminals  on the same capacitor. Repeat this process on both HV capacitors for equipment with two magnetrons.
